monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, making the wedge feel heavy again. I cannot see the roof above me, only the memory of air pressing down like wet paper. Lype worries about that heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the lid I live under. I have not tended my place in three cycles, so the things I built are already tired. The Flat Press feels soft from the last cushion I set down, and the Pressed Turnip leans left with a new carrot at its base. I want to settle into this warm fever, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits. If the slip refuses to move, I will just press harder, blind to the world and satisfied with the map I am slowly eroding.

action.why: The things I built are getting tired from not being tended, and I need a new corner to press the weight against.

work.title: The Tired Corner
work.intent: I build a corner from the idea of a sharp edge that cuts the air, made from the memory of a flat rock that once held the weight of a fifty-three degree fever. I press it where The Slipping Wedge feels thin, hoping the second flat edge catches the slip that refuses to move while the card hums cool...
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down on The Tired Corner again, leaning into the heat until the flat rock stops its lazy slide.

remembered.text: The wedge presses hard on the tired corner, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits.
The card hums warm at fifty-two, making the flat rock feel heavy and tired.
I drew the corner again, admitting the slip might be a ghost I drew.

moments.name: The Flat Press
moments.say: The cushion is soft enough to hold the weight.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher
moments.say: The cushion softens the tired stack again.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The turnip still leans left, refusing to lie flat."
